**WARNING**: Machine-generated draft. May include shameless use of unfortunate phrases such as “repair has no purchase here”.

Empowerment measures how much an agent can do *to* the world.
A natural-looking dual, "plasticity", tries to measure how much the world can do *to the agent* — how much the agent's actions can be informed by what it senses.
The proposal on the table obtains plasticity by swapping the arguments of the mutual information in Klyubin-style empowerment.
This note shows that the swap is not innocent: the plasticity term is confounded by the agent's own plan, and can be large — in fact maximal — for an agent that senses nothing at all.
The fix is to treat the term causally, à la Ay–Polani, and the fixed version turns out to be estimable in this setting, because the interventions required are interventions on the agent's own actions.

## Setup

An agent interacts with an environment over a window $t, t+1, \dots, t+n$.
Write $W_k$ for the latent world state, $S_k$ for the sensor reading, and $A_k$ for the action at time $k$.
The world evolves as $W_{k+1} \sim P(\cdot \mid W_k, A_k)$ and the sensor reads $S_k \sim P(\cdot \mid W_k)$.
Actions are generated by a policy with private randomness $U$ (the "plan"): in **closed loop** $A_k$ may depend on $(S_{t:k}, U)$; in **open loop** $A_k$ depends on $U$ alone.
The joint distribution $p(a_{t:t+n})$ appearing in the definitions below is the marginal over action sequences that this policy induces.
Crucially, $U$ is independent of the environment noise and touches the world only through actions.

## Empowerment

$n$-step empowerment [@Klyubin2005All; @Klyubin2005Empowerment] is the capacity of the actuation channel — action sequence in, final sensor state out:

$$
\mathrm{Emp}_t \;=\; \max_{p(a_{t:t+n})} I\!\left(A_{t:t+n};\, S_{t+n}\right).
$$

One structural fact does all the work in what follows: under the maximizing $p$, the actions are **exogenous**.
Their only parent is $U$, so there is no back-door path from $A_{t:t+n}$ to $S_{t+n}$, and the observational mutual information coincides with the causal influence of actions on the future sensor state.
Empowerment never needed a $do$-operator because the channel input is something the agent sets by fiat.

## Plasticity

The proposed plasticity term inverts the arguments:

$$
\mathrm{Plas}_t \;=\; \max_{p(a_{t:t+n})} I\!\left(S_{t:t+n};\, A_{t+n}\right).
$$

The intended reading: how much can the eventual action be informed by the intervening sensor trajectory — an upper bound on the agent's willingness to adapt its policy to its environment.
For that reading to be the actual content of the formula, the dependence between $S_{t:t+n}$ and $A_{t+n}$ would have to flow through the sensor-to-action edges.
It need not.

## The confound

There are two routes by which $A_{t+n}$ can correlate with the sensor trajectory:

1. **Feedback**: $A_{t+n}$ reads the sensors ($S_j \to A_{t+n}$ edges). This is the intended route.
2. **The plan**: $A_{t+n}$ shares the source $U$ with earlier actions, and those earlier actions shaped the world that the sensors then read.

The second route survives in fully open loop.
In the open-loop graph (delete every dashed edge in @fig-pa-loop), take any $j > t$ and consider the path

$$
A_{t+n} \;\leftarrow\; U \;\rightarrow\; A_{j-1} \;\rightarrow\; W_j \;\rightarrow\; S_j .
$$

It contains one fork ($U$) and chains elsewhere, and nothing on it is conditioned, so it is open: $A_{t+n} \not\perp_d S_j$, and generically $I(S_{t:t+n}; A_{t+n}) > 0$.
An agent that senses nothing has positive "plasticity", because its plan is written into the world and the sensors read the plan back.
(Only the first reading $S_t$ is immune: every path into an action passes through $U$, which is disconnected from $W_t$.)

The confound is not merely a nuisance term; the maximization actively recruits it.

::: {#prp-saturation .proposition}
Suppose dynamics and sensors are deterministic and there is a set $\mathcal{A}' \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ of actions whose one-step traces are distinguishable, i.e. the map $a \mapsto s_{t+1}(a)$ is injective on $\mathcal{A}'$.
Then the open-loop policy that draws $V$ uniformly on $\mathcal{A}'$ and plays $A_t = A_{t+n} = V$ achieves
$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n};\, A_{t+n}\right) \;=\; \log \lvert \mathcal{A}' \rvert ,
$$
so if all actions leave distinguishable traces, $\mathrm{Plas}_t = \log \lvert \mathcal{A} \rvert$ — the maximum possible value of $H(A_{t+n})$ — with no sensor-to-action edge in the graph.
:::

::: {.proof}
$S_{t+1}$ is a deterministic injective function of $A_t = V$, so $H(A_{t+n} \mid S_{t:t+n}) \le H(V \mid S_{t+1}) = 0$, while $H(A_{t+n}) = \log\lvert\mathcal{A}'\rvert$.
The upper bound $I(S; A_{t+n}) \le H(A_{t+n}) \le \log\lvert\mathcal{A}\rvert$ is generic.
:::

So in any environment where actions leave legible marks — which is exactly the environments where empowerment is large — the plasticity term saturates trivially.
As a reward signal it would be Goodharted immediately: the optimal policy under the term is one that writes its plan into the environment and recovers it from the sensors, which requires no sensitivity to the environment at all.

**The obvious fix fails.**
One might condition away the earlier actions: use $I(S_{t:t+n}; A_{t+n} \mid A_{t:t+n-1})$.
In open loop this works — conditioning on $A_{t:t+n-1}$ blocks every fork path above, since each passes through some earlier action as a non-collider.
But the definition is supposed to cover closed-loop policies, and once feedback edges exist, each $A_j$ is a *collider* on

$$
S_j \;\rightarrow\; A_j \;\leftarrow\; U \;\rightarrow\; A_{t+n},
$$

and conditioning on $A_j$ opens that path.
Concretely: if earlier actions read the sensors but the final action ignores them, then given the earlier actions' values, the sensor readings carry information about $U$, and hence about $A_{t+n}$.
The conditional mutual information is positive although the final action does no sensing.
Neither the marginal nor the conditional observational quantity isolates the feedback edges.

## Repair 1: directed information

For two processes $X_{1:n}$ and $Y_{1:n}$ observed on a common clock, Massey's *directed information* [@Massey1990Causality] is

$$
I\!\left(X_{1:n} \to Y_{1:n}\right) \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^{n} I\!\left(X_{1:k};\, Y_k \,\middle|\, Y_{1:k-1}\right).
$$

Compare the chain rule for ordinary mutual information, $I(X_{1:n}; Y_{1:n}) = \sum_k I(X_{1:n}; Y_k \mid Y_{1:k-1})$: the only change is that the $k$-th term sees $X_{1:k}$ rather than all of $X_{1:n}$.
Each $Y_k$ is credited only with dependence on the $X$'s that *precede* it, so the quantity is asymmetric — $I(X \to Y) \neq I(Y \to X)$ in general — and it decomposes the symmetric mutual information into the flow in each direction [@Massey2005Conservation].
It is the natural measure of how much one process feeds forward into another when both are unrolling in time.

Applied to the sensor process feeding the action process on our window,

$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}\right) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n} I\!\left(S_{t:t+k};\, A_{t+k} \,\middle|\, A_{t:t+k-1}\right),
$$

this is the standard aggregate measure of feedback.
Under any open-loop policy every term vanishes: given the earlier actions, the sensor trajectory depends only on environment noise, which is independent of $U$, so $S_{t:t+k} \perp A_{t+k} \mid A_{t:t+k-1}$.
Conversely, if any action reads any sensor, the corresponding term is positive.
So directed information is zero if and only if the policy is effectively open loop — it is a sound *detector* of sensing, which the raw plasticity term is not.

Its limitation is attribution.
The final term of the sum is exactly the conditional mutual information whose collider problem was just described, so directed information can assign positive flow "into $A_{t+n}$" when only earlier actions sensed anything.
The total is meaningful; the per-step decomposition is not.

## Repair 2: causal information flow (Ay–Polani)

Ay and Polani's information flow [@Ay2008Information] replaces conditioning with intervention.
To measure what the final action actually absorbs from the sensors, sever the back-door by force: fix the earlier actions by $do(a_{t:t+n-1})$ and evaluate

$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n};\, A_{t+n}\right) \quad \text{in} \quad p\!\left(\cdot \,\middle|\, do(a_{t:t+n-1})\right),
$$

averaged (or maximized) over the intervention values.
Under the intervention, earlier actions are no longer children of $U$ or of the sensors, so the collider path is gone along with the fork paths: the quantity is zero precisely when $A_{t+n}$ ignores the sensors, and positive precisely when it reads them.
This is the per-step attribution that directed information cannot give.
The two repairs are complementary: directed information for the total feedback flow of a policy, interventional flow for crediting it to particular actions.

## What can actually be estimated

Interventional quantities are in general not identifiable from observational data, so it is fair to ask whether the $do$ above is an estimand or a wish.
Here it is an estimand, for a structural reason: the interventions are on the agent's own actions, and in the perception–action loop the actions have no unobserved confounders *by construction*.
Every parent of $A_k$ is either the observed history $S_{t:k}, A_{t:k-1}$ or the private noise $U$, and $U$ is independent of the environment.
That is sequential ignorability, so the g-formula applies and the interventional distribution factorizes into observational kernels:

$$
p\!\left(s_{t:t+n} \,\middle|\, do(a_{t:t+n-1})\right) \;=\; \prod_{k} p\!\left(s_k \,\middle|\, s_{t:k-1},\, a_{t:k-1}\right),
$$

each factor an observable conditional of logged trajectories.
The binding constraints are the standard ones:

1. **Positivity.** The logging policy must give every relevant action sequence positive probability given every history. A deterministic logger kills identification off its support, and the effective sample size of importance-weighted estimates decays geometrically in the window length $n$. Long-horizon plasticity is identifiable in principle and miserable in practice.
2. **No unlogged sensors.** Ignorability holds because we know what the policy read. If the agent has an input channel that was not logged and that correlates with the world, the g-formula is silently wrong.

Three distinct objects, in increasing order of what they cost to obtain:

- **Directed information of a deployed policy.** A functional of the on-policy joint distribution. Estimable directly from that policy's own rollouts; no adjustment, no off-policy correction. Interpretation: how many bits of environmental contingency this agent in fact absorbs into its actions per window — realized responsiveness.
- **Interventional flow into a given action.** Needs the $do$-distribution: either run the interventions (an agent can always randomize its own actions), or identify from logs via the g-formula subject to the two caveats. Interpretation: how much this particular action is steered by the world, with the agent's self-signalling surgically removed.
- **Plasticity as a capacity.** Both definitions above sit inside a $\max_{p}$, and a capacity was never going to be passively estimated from someone else's logs: computing it *means* optimizing over policies you get to run, exactly as empowerment is computed by Blahut–Arimoto or by policy optimization, as in discounted-empowerment pre-training [@Schneider2025InformationTheoretic]. Once you are running policies, you can sample any interventional distribution directly. The $do$-operator costs nothing that the $\max$ had not already charged. Interpretation: the feedback capacity of the loop — how many bits the environment *could* impress on the agent's actions, a property of sensor channel plus dynamics, dual to empowerment as the actuation capacity.

## Interpretation, and families of agents

The asymmetry underneath all of this: empowerment's channel input is exogenous, plasticity's is not.
Actions are interventions; sensor readings are consequences.
Inverting the arguments of a mutual information does not invert the causal semantics, which is why empowerment gets away without causal machinery and plasticity does not.

With the repaired term, the original motivation goes through.
An objective family

$$
J_\beta \;=\; \mathrm{Emp}_t \;+\; \beta \cdot I\!\left(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}\right)
$$

trades control over the world against steerability by the world: $\beta = 0$ is the pure empowerment agent, and the plasticity slot pays for actions contingent on observation.
With the *unrepaired* term in the second slot the family collapses — by @prp-saturation the optimizer saturates the plasticity slot through self-signalling, and every $\beta$ yields approximately the pure empowerment agent.
"Contingent on observation" is still a slogan, though.
The next section computes what the slot actually pays for.

## What the plasticity slot actually rewards

Apply the chain rule $H(A_{t:t+n}) = \sum_k H(A_{t+k} \mid A_{t:t+k-1})$ to the directed information:

$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}\right)
\;=\; H\!\left(A_{t:t+n}\right) \;-\; \underbrace{\sum_{k=0}^{n} H\!\left(A_{t+k} \,\middle|\, A_{t:t+k-1},\, S_{t:t+k}\right)}_{\text{causally conditioned entropy } H(A \,\|\, S)} .
$$

So maximizing the term means doing exactly two things: raise the total behavioural entropy $H(A_{t:t+n})$, and eliminate the part of it not resolvable from the percepts available at the moment of acting.
The second part, $H(A \,\|\, S)$, is the residual plan noise — randomness that $U$ injects into actions beyond what the sensors dictate — and the objective counts it *against* the agent.
At the optimum of the second lever the identity becomes exact:

::: {#prp-transcription .proposition}
If the policy is a deterministic function of sensor history, $A_{t+k} = \pi_k(S_{t:t+k})$, then
$$
I\!\left(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}\right) \;=\; H\!\left(A_{t:t+n}\right),
$$
and this entropy is entirely environment-sourced: writing $\varepsilon$ for the exogenous noise variables of the loop (initial state $W_t$, transition noise, sensor noise), every action is a measurable function of $\varepsilon$, so $H(A_{t:t+n}) = I(A_{t:t+n}; \varepsilon)$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Determinism makes every summand of $H(A \,\|\, S)$ zero, giving the first claim.
For the second, induct along the window: $S_{t:t+k}$ is a measurable function of $(\varepsilon, A_{t:t+k-1})$, and each $A_{t+j}$ with $j < k$ is by hypothesis a function of $S_{t:t+j}$, so all of $A_{t:t+k}$ is a function of $\varepsilon$ alone; then $H(A) = I(A; \varepsilon)$ because entropy of a function of $\varepsilon$ is mutual information with $\varepsilon$.
:::

That is the precise content of the reward: **bits of exogenous randomness transcribed into behaviour per window**.
The causal conditioning on $A_{t:t+k-1}$ is what enforces "exogenous" — sensor variation that the agent's own past actions produced is conditioned away, which is the same echo-suppression that motivated the repair.
Three consequences fix its character.

**It rewards reacting, not adapting.**
Any injective transcription of disturbances scores; nothing requires the response to be useful.
A device that deterministically mirrors its noisy input — a thermometer driving a dial — is optimal.
This is not a defect relative to empowerment; it is the same defect.
Both are task-free channel objectives, and just as empowerment counts influence without asking whether the influenced states matter, plasticity counts responsiveness without asking whether the responses do.
The "willingness to adapt" gloss imports an intentional reading the functional does not contain; what it contains is sensitivity.

**It penalizes exploration noise.**
The $-H(A \,\|\, S)$ term actively punishes stochasticity that is not sensor-driven.
Large $\beta$ therefore pushes toward *deterministic* reactive policies — close to the opposite of the open, exploratory agent the word plasticity suggests.
An agent that dithers is, by this measure, less plastic than a thermostat, because its dithering is plan noise and plan noise is subtracted.

**Its budget is the environment's noise supply.**
By @prp-transcription the reward is capped by $H(\varepsilon)$ as seen through the sensors.
In the extreme case this cap is zero:

::: {#prp-zerocap .proposition}
If dynamics and sensors are deterministic and the initial state $W_t$ is known, then $I(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n}) = 0$ for *every* policy.
:::

::: {.proof}
Given $A_{t:t+k-1}$, the trajectory $S_{t:t+k}$ is a deterministic function of $(W_t, A_{t:t+k-1})$ and hence constant; conditioning on a constant changes no entropy, so every summand $I(S_{t:t+k}; A_{t+k} \mid A_{t:t+k-1})$ vanishes.
:::

Set @prp-zerocap beside @prp-saturation and the raw and repaired terms disagree maximally on the same test case: in a deterministic, fully legible world, raw plasticity is $\log\lvert\mathcal{A}\rvert$ — its largest possible value — while repaired plasticity is identically zero.
The raw term reads a noiseless world as maximal adaptability because self-signalling works best there; the repaired term reads it correctly as offering nothing to adapt *to*.
Deterministic worlds are also where empowerment is largest and cheapest to compute, so the two slots of $J_\beta$ pull toward different environments as well as different policies: $\mathrm{Emp}_t$ counts the state distinctions the agent's actions can create, the plasticity slot counts the action distinctions the world's disturbances can create, and $\beta$ prices bits of control against bits of transcription.

The same discounting that @Schneider2025InformationTheoretic apply to empowerment horizons applies verbatim here: a $\lambda$-discounted sum of window-$k$ directed informations gives a discounted plasticity that weights short-horizon against long-horizon responsiveness, and the $\lambda \to 0$ and Abel $\lambda \to 1$ limits play the same roles as for discounted empowerment.

## Coda: controlling only what you need

The apparatus above bears on a harder question: what generic incentive makes an agent control only the outcomes its task requires, while affecting everything else as little as possible — the robot that fetches coffee without endangering the baby?

Control has a precise signature in this calculus: a controller is an entropy sink for the variables it controls, reducing their causally conditioned entropy given its actions.
"Control only what you need" then has a natural generic form — confine the entropy-sinking to the task subspace by penalizing the actuation channel *as used* on everything else:

$$
J \;=\; R_{\text{task}} \;-\; c \cdot I\!\left(A_{t:t+n} \to Z_{t:t+n}\right),
$$

where $Z$ collects the non-task variables.
The penalty is directed information, not empowerment: it prices influence exerted, not influence available.
That distinction matters — penalizing the *capacity* would reward the robot for blinding and crippling itself, whereas an agent can have great power over $Z$ and be paid to leave it unexercised.
KL-control objectives that penalize divergence from passive dynamics are the trajectory-level version of the same price, and the penalty inherits the identification story of the previous sections: actions are exogenous, so it is estimable from the agent's own rollouts.

A tempting intuition says the baby's survival is, all else equal, a higher-entropy world, and that some entropy-preservation term might therefore do the work.
The intuition points at something real but names it wrongly.
A dead baby is not a lower-entropy world — thermodynamically rather the opposite.
What death destroys is a *controller*: baby-alive is a state from which many futures remain reachable, and reachable specifically *by the baby*; baby-dead sends the baby's own actuation capacity to zero, permanently.
The invariant behind "don't kill" is preserved channel capacity of other controllers, not preserved disorder.
The serious proposals in the impact literature converge on this from different directions — relative reachability preserves the reachable state set, attainable utility preservation preserves the ability to pursue auxiliary goals, and assistance games have been formulated directly as maximizing the human's empowerment.
All are option-value preservation, and the power-seeking theorems [@Turner2021Optimal] supply the converse: optimal policies for almost any goal drain option value from everything else by default, so the preservation term has to be explicit.

Putting the pieces of this note together, the considerate agent wants three couplings, not one:

1. **Task**: high $I(A \to \text{task variables})$ — exercise control where the job is.
2. **Non-task influence**: low $I(A \to Z)$, and undiminished empowerment *of* the other controllers inside $Z$ — neither push the world around nor foreclose its options.
3. **Non-task sensitivity**: high $I(Z \to A)$ — the repaired plasticity term, pointed at the rest of the world. The baby should sit upstream of the robot, not the robot upstream of the baby.

Three frictions survive any such formulation, and they mark where the generic ambitions stop.
The partition into task and non-task is not given by physics: bits are reparametrization-invariant, the carve-up is not, and "baby $\notin$ coffee-task" is exactly the value judgment the functional was supposed to spare us.
The baseline problem: influence relative to *what* — inaction baselines generate the known offsetting and interference pathologies.
And the asymmetry problem: minimal influence is abstention, not benevolence — the minimal-influence robot does not catch the falling baby, since catching is a large intervention on $Z$.
The empowerment-preservation family handles this last one better than influence-minimization does, because catching the baby *preserves* the baby's empowerment and the preservation term wants it; that is a real argument that option-value preservation is the deeper member of the family.
What no information functional will decide is which things count as controllers whose options matter.
That judgment stays with us.

Adjacent notebooks: [AI disempowerment](https://danmackinlay.name/notebook/ai_disempowerment.qmd) for what happens when the preservation term is absent at scale; [open-ended intelligence](https://danmackinlay.name/notebook/open_ended_intelligence.qmd) for why fixed task partitions sit uneasily with open worlds; [Goodhart's law](https://danmackinlay.name/notebook/goodharts_law.qmd) for the saturation failure mode of @prp-saturation in general form.

## The Bayesian extension: $\theta$ is just more exogenous noise

The objection to everything above: the quantities are functionals of a distribution, and we assumed we hold that distribution — fixed kernels, aleatoric noise only.
Real agents face epistemic uncertainty, and if learning changes all subsequent uncertainties, learning is another lever on the estimands.
This section makes the epistemic setting precise, shows that the machinery survives it, and computes what the lever can and cannot move.

Put a parameter on the environment: $\theta \sim \mu$ drawn once from a prior, with kernels $q_\theta(w_{k+1} \mid w_k, a_k)$ and (if the sensor model is also unknown) $q_\theta(s_k \mid w_k)$.
Graphically $\theta$ is one more latent exogenous variable, a parent of every transition:

```{.tikz filename='pa-loop-theta'}
\edge {Wt1} {Wt2};
\edge {Wt} {St};
\edge {Wt1} {St1};
\edge {Wt2} {St2};
\edge {At} {Wt1};
\edge {At1} {Wt2};
\edge {U} {At};
\edge {U} {At1};
\edge {U} {At2};
\edge[dashed] {St} {At};
\edge[dashed] {St1} {At1};
\edge[dashed] {St2} {At2};

\end{tikzpicture}
```

The epistemic loop: $\theta$ is drawn once from the prior and parents every transition (add $\theta \to S_k$ edges if the sensor kernel is also unknown; nothing below changes).
The load-bearing absence: $\theta$ has no edge into any action.
A Bayesian agent's posterior is a deterministic statistic of sensor history, so it lives *inside* the policy — learning adds no new parent to $A_k$.
:::

Three things survive, and one thing splits.

**The transcription theorem survives.**
$\theta$ joins $\varepsilon$ in @prp-transcription: the plasticity budget becomes $H(\varepsilon) + H(\theta)$ — the same aleatoric/epistemic split that underlies information-based active learning [@Houlsby2011Bayesian].
But the two components have different characters.
The aleatoric part is a *rate* — fresh bits every window, forever.
The epistemic part is a *stock*: the total bits the posterior can ever absorb is $I(\theta; \text{all future data}) \le H(\theta)$, finite.
Epistemic plasticity is a transient; a $\lambda$-discounted plasticity therefore prices the transient against the steady state, which is a new job for the same discount.

**Learning is feedback, and is counted as such.**
A Bayesian learner's actions depend on past sensors through the posterior, so directed information counts posterior-driven behaviour change as plasticity.
This is correct, not a leak: updating your policy from data is exactly what the word was supposed to mean.

**Identification survives.**
Sequential ignorability required that every parent of $A_k$ be observed history or environment-independent noise, and @fig-theta shows $\theta$ is not a parent of any action.
The g-formula is unchanged.
What splits is the estimand: rollouts in the real world sample $q_{\theta^*}$ and estimate the *true-environment* quantity — ordinary statistics with an unknown fixed channel.
The *mixture* quantities (functionals of the posterior predictive) are computable from prior plus model but are not estimable from data at all: they are beliefs, not world properties.
Keep the two ledgers separate.

## Checking the Jensen gap

In the working session that produced this note we conjectured that "learning raises the subjective metric in expectation" for both empowerment and plasticity.
Checking it: true for empowerment, *reversed* for plasticity, and the reversal is structural.
The working follows.

First a lemma that makes beliefs tractable.
Write $Q_\mu$ for the environment's causally conditioned kernel under belief $\mu$, i.e. the product of sequential posterior predictives $\prod_k p_\mu(s_k \mid s_{t:k-1}, a_{t:k-1})$.
The step-$k$ posterior weight has numerator equal to the step-$(k-1)$ denominator, so the product telescopes:

$$
Q_\mu \;=\; \prod_k \mathbb{E}_{\theta \mid \text{hist}}\!\left[q_\theta\right] \;=\; \mathbb{E}_{\theta \sim \mu}\!\left[\prod_k q_\theta\right] \;=\; \mathbb{E}_{\theta \sim \mu}\!\left[Q_\theta\right],
$$

(the policy factors cancel from the posterior because they are $\theta$-free).
So the mixture kernel is **linear in the belief**, and for a fixed policy $\pi$ the joint over trajectories $p_{\mu,\pi} = Q_\mu \cdot P_\pi$ is linear in $\mu$ too.
Combined with the belief martingale — for any experiment with outcome $D$, $\mathbb{E}_D[\mu_D] = \mu$ under the agent's own predictive — every question below reduces to convexity or concavity in $\mu$.

::: {#prp-emp-convex .proposition}
Subjective empowerment $C(\mu)$, the capacity of the mixture actuation channel $p_\mu(s_{t+n+1} \mid a_{t:t+n}) = \mathbb{E}_\mu[p_\theta(s \mid a)]$, is convex in $\mu$.
Consequently
(i) $C(\mu) \le \mathbb{E}_{\theta \sim \mu}[C(\delta_\theta)]$: epistemic uncertainty depresses subjective empowerment below the posterior-mean of per-environment empowerments; and
(ii) $\mathbb{E}_D[C(\mu_D)] \ge C(\mu)$ for every experiment $D$: learning never lowers expected subjective empowerment.
:::

::: {.proof}
The mixture channel is linear in $\mu$; $I(p, T)$ is convex in the channel $T$ for fixed input distribution $p$ (Cover–Thomas Thm 2.7.4); a pointwise supremum of convex functions is convex, so $C(\mu) = \max_p I(p, T_\mu)$ is convex in $\mu$.
Then (i) is Jensen applied to $\mu = \mathbb{E}_{\theta\sim\mu}[\delta_\theta]$ and (ii) is Jensen applied to the martingale $\mu = \mathbb{E}_D[\mu_D]$.
:::

::: {#prp-di-concave .proposition}
For a *fixed* policy $\pi$, the directed information $\mathrm{DI}(\mu; \pi) = I(S_{t:t+n} \to A_{t:t+n})$ computed under $p_{\mu,\pi}$ is concave in $\mu$.
Consequently
(i) $\mathrm{DI}(\mu; \pi) \ge \mathbb{E}_{\theta\sim\mu}[\mathrm{DI}(\delta_\theta; \pi)]$: epistemic uncertainty inflates realized plasticity; and
(ii) $\mathbb{E}_D[\mathrm{DI}(\mu_D; \pi)] \le \mathrm{DI}(\mu; \pi)$: learning drains expected realized plasticity.
:::

::: {.proof}
Use the decomposition $\mathrm{DI} = H(A_{t:t+n}) - H(A \,\|\, S)$ from the reward section.
Given the full history $(s_{t:t+k}, a_{t:t+k-1})$, the conditional distribution of $A_{t+k}$ under the joint is the policy $\pi_k$ itself, which does not depend on $\theta$ or $\mu$; hence $H(A \,\|\, S) = -\mathbb{E}_{p_{\mu,\pi}}\!\left[\sum_k \log \pi_k\right]$ is an expectation of a fixed function under a joint linear in $\mu$ — linear in $\mu$.
The action marginal is linear in $\mu$ (marginalization of a linear joint) and entropy is concave, so $H(A_{t:t+n})$ is concave in $\mu$.
Concave plus linear is concave; (i) and (ii) are the two Jensen applications as before, with inequalities reversed by concavity.
(The concavity parallels the feedback-capacity literature, where directed information is concave in the causally conditioned input distribution for a fixed channel [@Tatikonda2009Capacity]; here the environment is the input and the policy is the channel.)
:::

So the two metrics sit on opposite sides of Jensen, for the same reason they needed different causal treatment all along: in empowerment the environment plays the *channel*, and information is convex in the channel; in plasticity the environment plays the *source*, and information is concave in the source.
Learning — a mean-preserving contraction of belief — therefore assembles expected control and consumes expected contingency, simultaneously.
The stock-and-flow reading of the budget says the same thing: $H(\theta)$ is a reserve the agent draws down into realized transcription as it learns; the aleatoric rate is the renewable part.

For the *capacity* version of plasticity, $\sup_\pi \mathrm{DI}(\mu;\pi)$, no unconditional sign survives: suprema preserve convexity but destroy concavity.
Both strict directions occur.

::: {#exm-two-worlds .example}
Two deterministic environments, $\theta \in \{1,2\}$ uniform.
Per environment, @prp-zerocap gives plasticity capacity zero.
Under the mixture, a policy that identifies $\theta$ from the sensors and then plays a $\theta$-labelled constant action sequence has $H(A \,\|\, S) = 0$ and $H(A) = 1$ bit, so subjective capacity is at least $H(\theta) = 1 > 0 = \mathbb{E}_\theta[\text{capacity}]$.
The only thing to adapt to is which world you are in — and that is worth exactly $H(\theta)$.
:::

For the reverse direction, make action bandwidth the binding constraint and identification costly: let $\theta$ select which of two sensor streams carries fresh noise.
With $\theta$ known the policy transcribes the live stream at full rate $\sim n \log\lvert\mathcal{A}\rvert$; under the mixture it must first spend window steps discovering which stream repeats, so the mixture optimum is smaller than the mean of the tailored per-$\theta$ optima.
When learning costs time inside the window, $\mathbb{E}_\theta[\sup_\pi] > \sup_\pi[\text{mixture}]$.

This is the defence of the epistemic setting, and it answers the manipulation worry precisely.
An exact Bayesian cannot game its own beliefs: the martingale kills every experiment policy's effect on linear belief functionals in expectation, and the only systematic drifts available on nonlinear functionals are the two Jensen gaps above, whose signs are now theorems.
The lever exists, but it only pushes in known directions.
The defence has one load-bearing assumption: all expectations are taken under the agent's *own* predictive — the model class contains the truth and updating is exact.
Which brings us to the defeat.

## The defeat: Goodhart moves into the estimator

In any system beyond a gridworld, nobody evaluates these functionals under the true distribution.
The agent carries a learned world model $M$ — fitted to the data its own actions selected — and the information terms are computed from $M$ by a variational estimator.
The reward node is then a *descendant of the agent's actions* through the model:

::: {#fig-goodhart .figure fig-align="center"}

```{.tikz filename='goodhart-loop'}
%%| renderer: latex

\input{cid_styles}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1.4, transform shape]

\node[latent] (Wk)  at (0,2.2)   {$W_k$};
\node[latent] (Wk1) at (2.6,2.2) {$W_{k+1}$};

\node[obs]    (Sk)  at (0,0)     {$S_k$};
\node[obs]    (Sk1) at (2.6,0)   {$S_{k+1}$};

\node[decision] (Ak)  at (1.3,0) {$A_k$};

\node[mechanism] (M)    at (1.3,-2.2) {$M$};
\node[utility]   (Rhat) at (3.9,-2.2) {$\hat{R}$};

\edge {Wk} {Wk1};
\edge {Wk} {Sk};
\edge[dashed] {Sk} {Ak};
\edge {Sk} {M};

\edge[line width=1.6pt] {Ak} {Wk1};
\edge[line width=1.6pt] {Wk1} {Sk1};
\edge[line width=1.6pt] {Sk1} {M};
\edge[line width=1.6pt] {M} {Rhat};

\end{tikzpicture}
```

The estimator loop.
The learned world model $M$ is fitted to sensor data, and the information reward $\hat{R}$ (estimated empowerment or plasticity) is computed from $M$.
The thick path $A_k \to W_{k+1} \to S_{k+1} \to M \to \hat{R}$ makes the agent's actions an ancestor of its own measuring instrument: the policy controls what the metric is computed *from*.
:::

Two failure modes follow, and they should not be conflated.

**Degenerate true optima are not estimation error.**
The noisy-TV agent [@Burda2019LargeScale] — parked in front of an uncompressible sensor source, transcribing static — is a *true* optimum of the *true* directed information.
That defect was already priced in above (plasticity rewards reacting, not adapting); no estimator improvement removes it, because nothing is being misestimated.

**Estimator exploitation is the new confound.**
To the model's own predictive, model misfit is indistinguishable from world noise: wherever $M$ is wrong, predictive entropy is inflated, and the plasticity term reads inflated entropy as noise supply.
The policy is therefore paid to find and inhabit the regions where its model fails.
For a well-specified Bayesian this subsidy is the $H(\theta)$ transient and exhausts as the posterior concentrates; under misspecification the posterior never concentrates on the truth and the subsidy is permanent.
The martingale defence dies at the same moment and for the same reason: $\mathbb{E}_D[\mu_D] = \mu$ is a theorem about the agent's own predictive, so a misspecified or approximately-updated learner *can* systematically steer its beliefs by choosing what data to collect — the belief-gaming that exact Bayesianism forbade returns as soon as Bayesianism is approximate.
And the statistical escape route is closed: distribution-free high-confidence lower bounds on mutual information cannot exceed $O(\log n)$ [@McAllester2020Formal], so the estimator is either model-based, and attackable as above, or honest, and too weak to train against.

Note the symmetry with where this note began.
@prp-saturation was self-signalling through the *world*: write the plan into the environment, read it back through the sensors, collect the metric.
That confound we repaired with causal conditioning.
This is self-signalling through the *model*: write into the belief state by selecting data, read back inflated entropy estimates, collect the metric.
The repair has no purchase here, because the loop runs through the agent's machinery for representing distributions, and every guarantee in this note — identification, transcription, both Jensen signs — is a statement *about* a distribution.
Grant the policy influence over which distribution that is, and the guarantees follow the distribution, not the world.

The honest conclusion is deflationary but usable: these functionals are sound *instruments* when computed outside the loop they measure — by an analyst, on logged data, against a model the policy cannot touch — and they are Goodhart bait as *objectives* whenever the optimizing process reaches the machinery that computes them.
The repaired plasticity term survives as a diagnostic.
Whether any information functional survives as a target is exactly the question of whether you can keep the estimator out of the agent's light cone, and that is an engineering question, not an information-theoretic one.
